## Details **How it works** - **Own history:** the longest suffix match within the request's prompt and output, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`. Same kernel layout as `ngram_gpu`. - **Cross-request corpus:** finished responses go into a GPU token ring (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, default 1M). A hash index on each request's last 2 and last 4 tokens returns up to 16 candidate positions. Each is verified and extended to its full suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix matching, and hash collisions or overwritten documents only cost a candidate. - **Frequency vote:** for each candidate match length, the candidates matching at least that long vote on the continuation, as in SuffixDecoding. The highest-scoring chain wins, ties going to the longer match; then the longer of the own-history and corpus matches wins. - **Adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification`): per-slot confidences, learned online by source, match length and position, let the runner trim slots that aren't worth verifying. - **Seeded requests** (explicit `seed`, temperature > 0) draft only from their own history, and adaptive verification verifies all of their slots. Under sampling, both the drafts and the number of verified slots change which tokens are drawn. Greedy requests keep the corpus. - **Ingestion:** one GPU program per (document, block). Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset and skips positions that a later document of the same batch overwrites. Every position is written by exactly one program, so the result is exact and order-independent even when a burst is larger than the ring. A 256 × 4,096-token burst at the default 1M ring takes 0.58 ms. - **TP consistency without collectives:** finished ids are ingested in sorted order, index inserts use `atomic_max` over `(document << 32 | position)`, and the statistics are integer counters. - **Memory at the defaults:** 36 MB (4 MB corpus plus a 32 MB index). Suffix decoding also keeps the runner's token history on the GPU (`max_num_seqs × max_model_len × 4` bytes, e.g. 32 MiB at 256 × 32K).
How a corpus lookup works (diagram) ``` Request history: ... "report" "the" "camera" "at" "the" "north" "gate" └──── last 4 ────┘ └─ last 2 ┘ 1) LOOK UP hash(last 4), hash(last 2) -> buckets, 8 slots each (slot = newest occurrence in each of the last 8 documents) 2) EXTEND BACKWARDS each candidate against the request (up to 24 tokens): request: report the camera at the north gate corpus: log: the camera at the north gate -> match length 6 stale or colliding candidate -> length 0, dropped 3) VOTE + DRAFT candidates matching >= L tokens vote on the next k tokens; the chain with the highest summed probability wins 4) COMPARE with the longest match in the request's own history; the longer match wins, empty slots get the last token ``` Ingestion when a request finishes: `[last 3 prompt tokens | response]` is appended to the ring, and each position with at least 2 (4) tokens before it in the document is indexed under them: `table[hash][doc % 8] = max(existing, (doc, pos))`.
**Why a hash index** | Index | Propose cost (L4) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Suffix tree (Arctic, V1) | CPU, per request | Host sync, so no MRV2 or async scheduling | | Suffix array (#52097) | 1.3–4.5 ms as an eager library call (prototype measurement on a shared L4); #52097 reports 0.4–1.9 ms with its CUDA-graph path (L20, k=16) | Background rebuilds, epochs and a CPU collective for TP | | Brute-force GPU scan | 0.3–1.2 ms at batch 128 (prototype measurement) | Exact; cost grows with batch × corpus | | **Hash index + vote (this PR)** | **11–35 µs** GPU time for batch 1–256 (CUDA-graph microbenchmark), the same at 1M and 4M corpus tokens. As the engine runs it (eagerly): 89–95 µs per step at 4K context for batch 1–256, 231 µs at 128K context with 32 requests (`ngram_gpu`: 75–78 and 111 µs) | No rebuilds. The index alone is within 0.4% of an exact longest-match search; with the vote, about 1% below exact search + vote | One difference from Arctic: corpus matches need at least 2 tokens (so `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` must be at least 2 for the corpus), while own-history matches can be 1. Storing the last 3 prompt tokens with each response lets a response's first tokens be drafted from the corpus. **Taken from #52097 and @zip95297's MRV2 port** (`zip95297/vllm-dev`, branch `zip95297/suffix-gpu-mrv2`): GPU cross-request matching with no host sync; an `on_requests_finished` hook in `finish_requests` that ingests from `RequestState` and skips preempted requests (from the MRV2 port); sorting finished ids for TP consistency; the replay-based acceptance evaluation. **Changes outside the speculator** - `SpeculativeConfig`: suffix's default `num_speculative_tokens` is `min(8, suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth)` on both runners. On V1 it caps Arctic's dynamic draft length; set 24 for the previous V1 behavior. - `AdaptiveVerificationManager.pinned_requests`: optional drafter hook. Pinned requests keep all their scheduled drafts and the budget is chosen around them. Only suffix decoding sets it (seeded sampled requests); other drafters are unaffected. - `warmup.py`: drafters with a `reset_state` method reset after MRV2's kernel warmup, so the warmup requests don't stay in the corpus. - `model_runner.py`: `set_sampling_states`, `on_requests_finished` and (with adaptive verification) `add_request` hooks, each called only if the speculator defines it; dense `all_token_ids` for suffix. **Limitations** - The corpus is shared across requests regardless of `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, like Arctic's global tree on V1 (documented; set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` to isolate). - Adaptive verification needs full CUDA graphs and an attention backend that replays variable-length decode batches. On L4 that is `TRITON_ATTN`: vLLM's FA2 backend declares uniform-batch support only. Until #61509 lands, its startup profiling also costs KV capacity, which matters at long context. - Under async scheduling a finished request can carry up to about 2k+1 tokens past the stop point into the corpus. ## Open questions 1. **Adaptive verification by default?** It is what makes suffix decoding pay off from concurrency 32 up. It isn't on by default here because it fails at startup on backends that can't replay variable-length decode graphs (FA2, the pre-Hopper default), so a default needs a fallback to off. Happy to add that here, or in a follow-up. 2. **Low-concurrency trimming.** Adaptive verification trims too much at low concurrency on small models: Qwen2.5-1.5B at concurrency 8 is 1.29x with it vs 1.47x verifying every slot (7B: 1.36x vs 1.32x). Tune it here (for example with a more optimistic prior) or later? 3. **Corpus default.** 4M tokens adds about 2–3% acceptance, but the index grows from 32 MB to 128 MB. 4. **Tokens past the stop point.** Pass the scheduler's final length down to ingestion? 5. **Arctic-only options** (`max_spec_factor`, `min_token_prob`) are ignored on V2 (documented). Warn as well? ## Follow-ups - Exclude filler slots from spec-decode metrics for GPU drafters (as #52097 does on V1 and its MRV2 branch does; see also #44056 and #50518). With adaptive verification, trimmed slots are still counted as drafted. - Index responses while they're still being generated. That may be why Arctic is ahead on the templated VLM workload. - CUDA-graph the propose path (@zip95297's bucketized draft graphs). - aarch64 benchmarks. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

With it, 7/8 in fp32 (one flip at a 0.0004-nat near-tie) and 2/8 in bf16 7B: the number of verified slots changes the batch shapes.
## Details **How it works** - **Own history:** the longest suffix match within the request's prompt and output, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`. Same kernel layout as `ngram_gpu`. - **Cross-request corpus:** finished responses go into a GPU token ring (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, default 1M). A hash index on each request's last 2 and last 4 tokens returns up to 16 candidate positions. Each is verified and extended to its full suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix matching, and hash collisions or overwritten documents only cost a candidate. - **Frequency vote:** for each candidate match length, the candidates matching at least that long vote on the continuation, as in SuffixDecoding. The highest-scoring chain wins, ties going to the longer match; then the longer of the own-history and corpus matches wins. - **Adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification`): per-slot confidences, learned online by source, match length and position, let the runner trim slots that aren't worth verifying. - **Seeded requests** (explicit `seed`, temperature > 0) draft only from their own history, and adaptive verification verifies all of their slots. Under sampling, both the drafts and the number of verified slots change which tokens are drawn. Greedy requests keep the corpus. - **Ingestion:** one GPU program per (document, block). Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset and skips positions that a later document of the same batch overwrites. Every position is written by exactly one program, so the result is exact and order-independent even when a burst is larger than the ring. A 256 × 4,096-token burst at the default 1M ring takes 0.58 ms. - **TP consistency without collectives:** finished ids are ingested in sorted order, index inserts use `atomic_max` over `(document << 32 | position)`, and the statistics are integer counters. - **Memory at the defaults:** 36 MB (4 MB corpus plus a 32 MB index). Suffix decoding also keeps the runner's token history on the GPU (`max_num_seqs × max_model_len × 4` bytes, e.g. 32 MiB at 256 × 32K).
How a corpus lookup works (diagram) ``` Request history: ... "report" "the" "camera" "at" "the" "north" "gate" └──── last 4 ────┘ └─ last 2 ┘ 1) LOOK UP hash(last 4), hash(last 2) -> buckets, 8 slots each (slot = newest occurrence in each of the last 8 documents) 2) EXTEND BACKWARDS each candidate against the request (up to 24 tokens): request: report the camera at the north gate corpus: log: the camera at the north gate -> match length 6 stale or colliding candidate -> length 0, dropped 3) VOTE + DRAFT candidates matching >= L tokens vote on the next k tokens; the chain with the highest summed probability wins 4) COMPARE with the longest match in the request's own history; the longer match wins, empty slots get the last token ``` Ingestion when a request finishes: `[last 3 prompt tokens | response]` is appended to the ring, and each position with at least 2 (4) tokens before it in the document is indexed under them: `table[hash][doc % 8] = max(existing, (doc, pos))`.
**Why a hash index** | Index | Propose cost (L4) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Suffix tree (Arctic, V1) | CPU, per request | Host sync, so no MRV2 or async scheduling | | Suffix array (#52097) | 1.3–4.5 ms as an eager library call (prototype measurement on a shared L4); #52097 reports 0.4–1.9 ms with its CUDA-graph path (L20, k=16) | Background rebuilds, epochs and a CPU collective for TP | | Brute-force GPU scan | 0.3–1.2 ms at batch 128 (prototype measurement) | Exact; cost grows with batch × corpus | | **Hash index + vote (this PR)** | **11–35 µs** GPU time for batch 1–256 (CUDA-graph microbenchmark), the same at 1M and 4M corpus tokens. As the engine runs it (eagerly): 89–95 µs per step at 4K context for batch 1–256, 231 µs at 128K context with 32 requests (`ngram_gpu`: 75–78 and 111 µs) | No rebuilds. The index alone is within 0.4% of an exact longest-match search; with the vote, about 1% below exact search + vote | One difference from Arctic: corpus matches need at least 2 tokens (so `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` must be at least 2 for the corpus), while own-history matches can be 1. Storing the last 3 prompt tokens with each response lets a response's first tokens be drafted from the corpus. **Taken from #52097 and @zip95297's MRV2 port** (`zip95297/vllm-dev`, branch `zip95297/suffix-gpu-mrv2`): GPU cross-request matching with no host sync; an `on_requests_finished` hook in `finish_requests` that ingests from `RequestState` and skips preempted requests (from the MRV2 port); sorting finished ids for TP consistency; the replay-based acceptance evaluation. **Changes outside the speculator** - `SpeculativeConfig`: suffix's default `num_speculative_tokens` is `min(8, suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth)` on both runners. On V1 it caps Arctic's dynamic draft length; set 24 for the previous V1 behavior. - `AdaptiveVerificationManager.pinned_requests`: optional drafter hook. Pinned requests keep all their scheduled drafts and the budget is chosen around them. Only suffix decoding sets it (seeded sampled requests); other drafters are unaffected. - `warmup.py`: drafters with a `reset_state` method reset after MRV2's kernel warmup, so the warmup requests don't stay in the corpus. - `model_runner.py`: `set_sampling_states`, `on_requests_finished` and (with adaptive verification) `add_request` hooks, each called only if the speculator defines it; dense `all_token_ids` for suffix. **Limitations** - The corpus is shared across requests regardless of `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, like Arctic's global tree on V1 (documented; set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` to isolate). - Adaptive verification needs full CUDA graphs and an attention backend that replays variable-length decode batches. On L4 that is `TRITON_ATTN`: vLLM's FA2 backend declares uniform-batch support only. Until #61509 lands, its startup profiling also costs KV capacity, which matters at long context. - Under async scheduling a finished request can carry up to about 2k+1 tokens past the stop point into the corpus. ## Open questions 1. **Adaptive verification by default?** It is what makes suffix decoding pay off from concurrency 32 up. It isn't on by default here because it fails at startup on backends that can't replay variable-length decode graphs (FA2, the pre-Hopper default), so a default needs a fallback to off. Happy to add that here, or in a follow-up. 2. **Low-concurrency trimming.** Adaptive verification trims too much at low concurrency on small models: Qwen2.5-1.5B at concurrency 8 is 1.29x with it vs 1.47x verifying every slot (7B: 1.36x vs 1.32x). Tune it here (for example with a more optimistic prior) or later? 3. **Corpus default.** 4M tokens adds about 2–3% acceptance, but the index grows from 32 MB to 128 MB. 4. **Tokens past the stop point.** Pass the scheduler's final length down to ingestion? 5. **Arctic-only options** (`max_spec_factor`, `min_token_prob`) are ignored on V2 (documented). Warn as well? ## Follow-ups - Exclude filler slots from spec-decode metrics for GPU drafters (as #52097 does on V1 and its MRV2 branch does; see also #44056 and #50518). With adaptive verification, trimmed slots are still counted as drafted. - Index responses while they're still being generated. That may be why Arctic is ahead on the templated VLM workload. - CUDA-graph the propose path (@zip95297's bucketized draft graphs). - aarch64 benchmarks. ---

+## Model Runner V2
+
+On Model Runner V2, `method: "suffix"` runs on the GPU, works with async scheduling and does not need Arctic Inference. It builds on [`ngram_gpu`](n_gram.md):
+
+- Each request is matched against its own prompt and output using the longest matching suffix, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` tokens, rather than a fixed n-gram window.
+- Responses of finished requests are kept in a GPU corpus (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, 1M tokens by default, oldest first out; `suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests: 0` disables it). Each step, every request looks up candidate positions in the corpus by its last 2 and last 4 tokens and extends them to the longest suffix match (so corpus matching needs `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` of at least 2); the continuation is chosen by how often each next token follows those matches.
+
+The longer match wins. The draft always has `num_speculative_tokens` tokens; slots without a match are filled with the last sampled token, and `suffix_decoding_max_spec_factor` and `suffix_decoding_min_token_prob` are not used. Without adaptive verification (below), Model Runner V2 verifies every slot, so keep `num_speculative_tokens` moderate (the default is `8`).
+
+Requests with an explicit `seed` that sample (`temperature > 0`) draft only from their own history, and adaptive verification verifies all of their draft slots: with sampling, the drafts and the number of verified slots affect which tokens are drawn, so this keeps their outputs independent of other requests. Greedy requests keep using the corpus.

+!!! warning "The corpus is shared"
+    Like the global suffix tree on V1, the corpus holds responses from all requests, whatever their `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, and any request can draft from it. Drafts never change the output distribution, but how many are accepted shows in decode speed. Where requests must not influence each other, set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0`.

+def _local_draft(hist, k, depth):
+    """Continuation of the longest, rightmost earlier occurrence of a suffix
+    of ``hist`` within ``hist`` (empty if no token matches)."""
+    best_len, best_pos = 0, 0
+    for i in range(1, len(hist)):
+        m = 0
+        while m < depth and i - 1 - m >= 0 and hist[i - 1 - m] == hist[-1 - m]:
+            m += 1
+        if m > 0 and (m, i) >= (best_len, best_pos):
+            best_len, best_pos = m, i
+    return [int(t) for t in hist[best_pos : best_pos + k]] if best_len else []
+

+def _follows_in_corpus(docs, hist, draft, n=2):
+    """Draft continues some occurrence of hist's last n tokens in a doc."""
+    tail = [int(t) for t in hist[-n:]]
+    for doc in docs:
+        for i in range(n, len(doc)):
+            if doc[i - n : i] == tail and doc[i : i + len(draft)] == draft:
+                return True
+    return False

+def _ref_ingest(state, docs, cap, num_buckets, slots=8):
+    """Python model of ingestion: documents placed one after another, wrapping
+    to 0 when they don't fit, each position indexed by its 2 and 4 tokens."""
+    corpus, table = state["corpus"], state["table"]
+    for doc in docs:

+        head, seq = state["head"], state["doc_seq"]
+        for j in range(n):

+            hv = 0
+            for d in range(4):
+                t = doc[j - 1 - d] if j - 1 - d >= 0 else 0
+                hv = _s64((hv ^ t) * _HASH_MUL)
+                b = ((hv >> 29) ^ hv) & (num_buckets - 1)
+                if (d == 1 and j >= 2) or (d == 3 and j >= 4):
+                    t_idx = (1 if d == 1 else 0, b, seq % slots)
+                    table[t_idx] = max(table[t_idx], (seq << 32) | (head + j))
+        corpus[head + n] = -1
+        state["head"] = head + n + 1

+"""GPU suffix decoding speculator for the V2 model runner.

+Extends the n-gram speculator with the two parts of SuffixDecoding

+* Variable-length matching: drafts continue the occurrence whose preceding
+  tokens match the longest suffix of the request's history (up to
+  ``suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth``), instead of a fixed n-gram window.
+* Cross-request memory: responses of finished requests are appended to a
+  device-resident token corpus. A hash index keyed on the last 2 and last 4
+  tokens gives candidate positions, and each candidate is extended to the
+  longest suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix
+  matching.
+

+    key_len = tl.where(is4, 4, 2)
+    slot = tl.where(
+        is4, bucket4 * SLOTS + c_iota, (NUM_BUCKETS + bucket2) * SLOTS + c_iota - SLOTS
+    )
+    vals = tl.load(table_ptr + slot)
+    cpos = vals & 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+    src_pos = cpos[:, None] - 1 - d_iota[None, :]
+    src = tl.load(
+        corpus_ptr + src_pos,
+        mask=(vals[:, None] >= 0) & (src_pos >= 0) & (d_iota[None, :] < MAX_DEPTH),
+        other=-1,
+    )
+    miss = (src != tail[None, :]).to(tl.int32)
+    c_len = tl.sum((tl.cumsum(miss, axis=1) == 0).to(tl.int64), axis=1)
+    nxt = tl.load(corpus_ptr + cpos, mask=(vals >= 0) & (cpos < corpus_len), other=-1)
+    ok = (vals >= 0) & (nxt >= 0) & (c_len >= key_len) & (seq_len >= key_len)
+    # Both buckets often hold the same position; count it once.
+    dup = (
+        (cpos[:, None] == cpos[None, :])
+        & ok[:, None]
+        & (c_iota[:, None] < c_iota[None, :])
+    )
+    ok = ok & (tl.max(dup.to(tl.int32), axis=0) == 0)
+
+    # Continuations, cut at the first document separator.
+    cont_pos = cpos[:, None] + k_iota[None, :]
+    cont = tl.load(
+        corpus_ptr + cont_pos,
+        mask=ok[:, None] & (k_iota[None, :] < K) & (cont_pos < corpus_len),
+        other=-1,
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    cont = tl.where(tl.cumsum((cont < 0).to(tl.int32), axis=1) == 0, cont, -1)
+
+    # Candidates sharing a match length draft identical chains; score each
+    # distinct length once.
+    same_len = (
+        (c_len[:, None] == c_len[None, :])
+        & ok[:, None]
+        & (c_iota[:, None] < c_iota[None, :])
+    )
+    first = ok & (tl.max(same_len.to(tl.int32), axis=0) == 0)
+
+    # A token's probability is its vote count over the candidates still
+    # alive, which is the previous token's count, so a chain's score
+    # telescopes to (sum of its vote counts) / (candidates at the start).
+    # Scores are compared as these integer fractions, so ties are exact.
+    best_num = tl.full((), -1, tl.int64)
+    best_den = tl.full((), 1, tl.int64)
+    best_len = tl.zeros((), tl.int64)
+    best_n = tl.zeros((), tl.int64)
+    best_chain = tl.zeros([K_PO2], tl.int64)
+    for i in range(C):
+        sel = c_iota == i
+        if tl.sum(tl.where(sel, first.to(tl.int32), 0), axis=0) > 0:
+            L = tl.sum(tl.where(sel, c_len, 0), axis=0)
+            alive = ok & (c_len >= L)
+            den = tl.maximum(tl.sum(alive.to(tl.int64), axis=0), 1)
+            go = L > 0
+            num = tl.zeros((), tl.int64)
+            n_emit = tl.zeros((), tl.int64)
+            chain = tl.zeros([K_PO2], tl.int64)
+            for d in tl.static_range(K):
+                col = tl.sum(tl.where(k_iota[None, :] == d, cont, 0), axis=1)
+                has = alive & (col >= 0)
+                cnt = tl.sum(
+                    ((col[:, None] == col[None, :]) & has[None, :]).to(tl.int32), axis=1
+                )
+                cnt = tl.where(has, cnt, 0)
+                cmax = tl.max(cnt, axis=0)
+                # Most frequent next token; ties go to the newest candidate.
+                newest = tl.max(tl.where(has & (cnt == cmax), vals, -1), axis=0)
+                next_tok = tl.sum(tl.where(has & (vals == newest), col, 0), axis=0)
+                go = go & (cmax > 0)
+                num = tl.where(go, num + cmax.to(tl.int64), num)
+                chain = tl.where((k_iota == d) & go, next_tok, chain)
+                n_emit += go.to(tl.int64)
+                alive = alive & has & (col == next_tok)
+            lhs = num * best_den
+            rhs = best_num * den
+            take = (lhs > rhs) | ((lhs == rhs) & (best_len < L))
+            best_num = tl.where(take, num, best_num)
+            best_den = tl.where(take, den, best_den)
+            best_len = tl.where(take, L, best_len)
+            best_n = tl.where(take, n_emit, best_n)
+            best_chain = tl.where(take, chain, best_chain)
+    return best_len, best_chain, best_n

+@triton.jit
+def _suffix_finalize_kernel(
+    token_ids_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs, token_ids_stride]
+    token_ids_stride,
+    idx_mapping_ptr,  # *int32  [B]
+    total_len_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]
+    num_sampled_ptr,  # *int32  [B]
+    last_sampled_ptr,  # *int64  [max_num_reqs]
+    scratch_ptr,  # *int64  [B, scratch_stride]
+    scratch_stride,
+    num_blocks,
+    Lp1,
+    corpus_ptr,  # *int32  [corpus_len]
+    corpus_len,
+    table_ptr,  # *int64  [2, NUM_BUCKETS, SLOTS]
+    drafts_ptr,  # *int64  [B, K]  (output)
+    num_valid_ptr,  # *int32  [B]  (output)
+    stats_ptr,  # *int64  [2 * _NUM_LEN_BUCKETS, K, 2]  (accepted, observed)
+    last_bucket_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]  (output)
+    last_valid_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]  (output)
+    conf_ptr,  # *fp32  [B, K]  (output)
+    seeded_ptr,  # *bool  [B]  seeded request sampled at temperature > 0
+    HAS_CORPUS: tl.constexpr,
+    ADAPTIVE: tl.constexpr,
+    HASH_MUL: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_BUCKETS: tl.constexpr,
+    SLOTS: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_DEPTH: tl.constexpr,
+    DEPTH_PO2: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    K_PO2: tl.constexpr,
+    NB_PO2: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    req = tl.load(idx_mapping_ptr + b).to(tl.int64)
+    seq_len = tl.load(total_len_ptr + req).to(tl.int64)
+    num_sampled = tl.load(num_sampled_ptr + b)
+    last_tok = tl.load(last_sampled_ptr + req)
+    row = token_ids_ptr + req * token_ids_stride
+
+    # Best match in the request's own history.
+    nb = tl.arange(0, NB_PO2).to(tl.int64)
+    l_score = tl.max(
+        tl.load(scratch_ptr + b * scratch_stride + nb, mask=nb < num_blocks, other=0),
+        axis=0,
+    )
+    l_len = l_score // Lp1
+    l_pos = l_score - l_len * Lp1
+
+    k_iota = tl.arange(0, K_PO2).to(tl.int64)
+    k_mask = k_iota < K
+    idx = l_pos + k_iota
+    draft_ok = k_mask & (idx < seq_len) & (l_len > 0)
+    draft = tl.load(row + idx, mask=draft_ok, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+
+    if HAS_CORPUS:
+        g_len, g_draft, g_n = _corpus_draft(
+            row,
+            seq_len,
+            table_ptr,
+            corpus_ptr,
+            corpus_len,
+            HASH_MUL,
+            NUM_BUCKETS,
+            SLOTS,
+            MAX_DEPTH,
+            DEPTH_PO2,
+            K,
+            K_PO2,
+        )
+        # The longer match wins; ties go to the request's own history.
+        # Corpus drafts change as other requests finish, and the rejection
+        # sampler's draws depend on the drafts, so seeded sampled requests
+        # draft only from their own history to stay reproducible.
+        seeded = tl.load(seeded_ptr + b).to(tl.int32)
+        use_corpus = (g_len > l_len) & (seeded == 0)
+        draft = tl.where(use_corpus, g_draft, draft)
+        draft_ok = tl.where(use_corpus, k_iota < g_n, draft_ok)
+        match_len = tl.where(use_corpus, g_len, l_len)
+        source = use_corpus.to(tl.int64)
+    else:
+        match_len = l_len
+        source = tl.zeros((), tl.int64)
+
+    draft_ok = draft_ok & (num_sampled > 0)
+    num_valid = tl.sum(draft_ok.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
+    # Invalid slots fall back to the last sampled token; they are verified as
+    # ordinary (rejectable) drafts, so the fill value only affects efficiency.
+    out = tl.where(draft_ok, draft, last_tok)
+    tl.store(drafts_ptr + b * K + k_iota, out, mask=k_mask)
+    tl.store(num_valid_ptr + b, num_valid)
+
+    if ADAPTIVE:
+        # Per-position confidence for adaptive verification: the observed
+        # acceptance rate for drafts like this one (Laplace-smoothed); filler
+        # slots get 0 so they are trimmed first.
+        bucket = source * _NUM_LEN_BUCKETS + _len_bucket(tl.maximum(match_len, 1))
+        stat = stats_ptr + (bucket * K + k_iota) * 2
+        accepted = tl.load(stat, mask=k_mask, other=0).to(tl.float32)
+        observed = tl.load(stat + 1, mask=k_mask, other=0).to(tl.float32)
+        conf = tl.where(draft_ok, (accepted + 1.0) / (observed + 2.0), 0.0)
+        tl.store(conf_ptr + b * K + k_iota, conf, mask=k_mask)
+        tl.store(
+            last_bucket_ptr + req, tl.where(num_valid > 0, bucket, -1).to(tl.int32)
+        )
+        tl.store(last_valid_ptr + req, num_valid)
+

+@triton.jit
+def _suffix_observe_kernel(
+    idx_mapping_ptr,  # *int32  [B]
+    num_sampled_ptr,  # *int32  [B]
+    num_rejected_ptr,  # *int32  [B]
+    stats_ptr,  # *int64  [2 * _NUM_LEN_BUCKETS, K, 2]
+    last_bucket_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]
+    last_valid_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    K_PO2: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Fold the target's verdict on each request's last draft into the stats.
+
+    Integer atomics are order-independent, so every TP rank keeps identical
+    stats (and therefore identical confidences).
+    """
+    b = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    req = tl.load(idx_mapping_ptr + b).to(tl.int64)
+    bucket = tl.load(last_bucket_ptr + req).to(tl.int64)
+    num_sampled = tl.load(num_sampled_ptr + b).to(tl.int64)
+    if (bucket < 0) | (num_sampled == 0):
+        return
+    num_accepted = num_sampled - 1
+    num_verified = num_accepted + tl.load(num_rejected_ptr + b).to(tl.int64)
+    num_valid = tl.load(last_valid_ptr + req).to(tl.int64)
+    k_iota = tl.arange(0, K_PO2).to(tl.int64)
+    # Accepted positions plus the first rejected one were observed.
+    observed = (
+        (k_iota < K)
+        & (k_iota <= num_accepted)
+        & (k_iota < num_verified)
+        & (k_iota < num_valid)
+    )
+    stat = stats_ptr + (bucket * K + k_iota) * 2
+    tl.atomic_add(stat, (k_iota < num_accepted).to(tl.int64), mask=observed)
+    tl.atomic_add(stat + 1, tl.full([K_PO2], 1, tl.int64), mask=observed)
+    tl.store(last_bucket_ptr + req, -1)
+

+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_docs"])
+def _suffix_ingest_kernel(
+    token_ids_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs, token_ids_stride]
+    token_ids_stride,
+    docs_ptr,  # *int32  [F, 2]  (slot, start) of finished requests, sorted
+    num_docs,
+    total_len_ptr,  # *int32  [max_num_reqs]
+    corpus_ptr,  # *int32  [corpus_len]
+    corpus_len,
+    head_ptr,  # *int64  [1]  next write offset
+    doc_seq_ptr,  # *int64  [1]  documents ingested so far
+    head_out_ptr,  # *int64  [1]
+    doc_seq_out_ptr,  # *int64  [1]
+    table_ptr,  # *int64  [2, NUM_BUCKETS, SLOTS]
+    HASH_MUL: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_BUCKETS: tl.constexpr,
+    SLOTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Append finished responses to the corpus ring and index them, with one
+    program per (document, block).
+
+    Documents are placed one after another. A document that does not fit
+    before the end of the ring wraps to offset 0, so no document straddles
+    the boundary. Older documents are overwritten in FIFO order (including
+    earlier documents of the same batch, if the batch exceeds the ring);
+    their index entries become stale and are rejected by verification at
+    lookup. Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset
+    and skips positions a later document of the batch overwrites, so every
+    position is written by exactly one program and the result does not
+    depend on execution order.
+    """
+    f = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    blk = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64)
+    cap = tl.cast(corpus_len, tl.int64)
+    req = tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * f).to(tl.int64)
+    end = tl.load(total_len_ptr + req).to(tl.int64)
+    # Keep the newest cap - 1 tokens of an over-long response.
+    start = tl.maximum(tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * f + 1).to(tl.int64), end - (cap - 1))
+    n = tl.maximum(end - start, 0)
+    # Block 0 also writes the separator.
+    if (blk > 0) & (blk * BLOCK >= n):
+        return
+    head = tl.load(head_ptr)
+    for i in range(f):
+        req_i = tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * i).to(tl.int64)
+        end_i = tl.load(total_len_ptr + req_i).to(tl.int64)
+        start_i = tl.maximum(
+            tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * i + 1).to(tl.int64), end_i - (cap - 1)
+        )
+        n_i = tl.maximum(end_i - start_i, 0)
+        head = tl.where(head + n_i + 1 > cap, 0, head) + n_i + 1
+    head = tl.where(head + n + 1 > cap, 0, head)
+    doc_seq = tl.load(doc_seq_ptr) + f
+
+    j = blk * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.int64)
+    m = j < n
+    pos = head + j
+    sep = head + n
+    keep = m
+    keep_sep = sep >= 0
+    later = head + n + 1
+    for g in range(f + 1, num_docs):
+        req_g = tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * g).to(tl.int64)
+        end_g = tl.load(total_len_ptr + req_g).to(tl.int64)
+        start_g = tl.maximum(
+            tl.load(docs_ptr + 2 * g + 1).to(tl.int64), end_g - (cap - 1)
+        )
+        n_g = tl.maximum(end_g - start_g, 0)
+        later = tl.where(later + n_g + 1 > cap, 0, later)
+        # Document g and its separator occupy [later, later + n_g].
+        keep = keep & ((pos < later) | (pos > later + n_g))
+        keep_sep = keep_sep & ((sep < later) | (sep > later + n_g))
+        later += n_g + 1
+    if blk == 0:
+        tl.store(corpus_ptr + sep, -1, mask=keep_sep)
+        if f == num_docs - 1:
+            tl.store(head_out_ptr, sep + 1)
+            tl.store(doc_seq_out_ptr, doc_seq + 1)
+
+    row = token_ids_ptr + req * token_ids_stride + start
+    tl.store(corpus_ptr + pos, tl.load(row + j, mask=m), mask=keep)
+    # Index each position j under its preceding 2 and 4 tokens, when they lie
+    # in the document. Entries order by (document, position), so atomic_max
+    # keeps the newest occurrence regardless of execution order.
+    slot = doc_seq % SLOTS
+    val = (doc_seq << 32) | pos
+    hv = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.int64)
+    for d in tl.static_range(4):
+        t = tl.load(row + j - 1 - d, mask=m & (j - 1 - d >= 0), other=0)
+        hv = (hv ^ t.to(tl.int64)) * HASH_MUL
+        if d == 1:
+            tl.atomic_max(
+                table_ptr + (NUM_BUCKETS + _bucket(hv, NUM_BUCKETS)) * SLOTS + slot,
+                val,
+                mask=m & (j >= 2),
+            )
+        if d == 3:
+            tl.atomic_max(
+                table_ptr + _bucket(hv, NUM_BUCKETS) * SLOTS + slot,
+                val,
+                mask=m & (j >= 4),
+            )

+class SuffixSpeculator(BaseSpeculator):
+    """V2-compatible GPU suffix decoding speculator."""
+
+    supports_mm_inputs = False
+    draft_logits = None
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        device: torch.device,
+        req_states: RequestState,
+    ):
+        if not HAS_TRITON:
+            raise RuntimeError("suffix speculative decoding requires Triton.")
+        spec = vllm_config.speculative_config
+        assert spec is not None
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self.device = device
+        self.req_states = req_states
+        self.num_speculative_steps: int = spec.num_speculative_tokens
+        self.max_depth: int = spec.suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth
+        self.max_num_reqs: int = vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_seqs
+        self.max_model_len: int = vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len
+
+        L = self.max_model_len
+        if L >= 1024:
+            self.block_l = 256
+        elif L >= 256:
+            self.block_l = 128
+        else:
+            self.block_l = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(max(L, 1)))
+        self.n_blocks = triton.cdiv(L, self.block_l)
+        self.scratch = torch.zeros(
+            (self.max_num_reqs, self.n_blocks), dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+
+        # Corpus of finished responses separated by -1, plus two hash tables
+        # keyed on the last 4 and last 2 tokens before each position. A
+        # capacity of 0 disables it.
+        self.corpus_len: int = (
+            spec.suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens
+            if spec.suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests != 0
+            else 0
+        )
+        if self.corpus_len > 0 and self.max_depth < 2:
+            # Corpus matches need the 2-token hash key.
+            logger.warning(
+                "suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth=%d is too short for "
+                "cross-request matching (needs >= 2); drafting from each "
+                "request's own history only.",
+                self.max_depth,
+            )
+            self.corpus_len = 0
+        self.has_corpus = self.corpus_len > 0
+        self.num_buckets = triton.next_power_of_2(max(16, self.corpus_len // 4))
+        self.corpus = torch.full(
+            (max(self.corpus_len, 1),), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        self.table = torch.full(
+            (2, self.num_buckets if self.has_corpus else 1, _BUCKET_SLOTS),
+            -1,
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        self.corpus_head = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        self.doc_seq = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        # Host mirror of doc_seq: index entries keep it in 31 bits.
+        self.num_docs = 0
+        self.ingest_out = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+
+        # Batch-ordered draft output, scattered into RequestState.draft_tokens
+        # by the model runner (same contract as the model-based speculators).
+        self.drafts = torch.zeros(
+            (self.max_num_reqs, self.num_speculative_steps),
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        # Number of real (non-filler) draft tokens per batch row.
+        self.num_valid = torch.zeros(
+            self.max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+
+        # Adaptive verification (optional): per-slot confidences from
+        # acceptance statistics learned online.
+        self.enable_adaptive_verification = spec.enable_adaptive_verification
+        self.draft_token_confidence_probs = torch.zeros(
+            (self.max_num_reqs, self.num_speculative_steps),
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        self.accept_stats = torch.zeros(
+            (2 * _NUM_LEN_BUCKETS, self.num_speculative_steps, 2),
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        self.last_bucket = torch.full(
+            (self.max_num_reqs,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        self.last_valid = torch.zeros(
+            self.max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        self.num_steps = 0
+        # Slots reassigned since the last propose; their stats bookkeeping
+        # still belongs to the previous request.
+        self.new_slots: list[int] = []
+        self.sampling_states: SamplingStates | None = None
+        self.not_seeded = torch.zeros(
+            self.max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.bool, device=device
+        )
+
+    def set_sampling_states(self, sampling_states: SamplingStates) -> None:
+        self.sampling_states = sampling_states
+
+    def seeded_requests(self, req_indices: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray | None:
+        """Mask of requests with an explicit seed that sample (temperature >
+        0), or None if there are none. Their drafts depend only on their own
+        history, so verifying all of their slots keeps them reproducible.
+        Greedy outputs don't depend on the drafts, so they keep the corpus."""
+        states = self.sampling_states
+        if states is None or not states.any_explicit_seed(req_indices):
+            return None
+        seeded = states.seeds_set[req_indices] & (
+            states.temperature.np[req_indices] != 0.0
+        )
+        return seeded if seeded.any() else None
+
+    def add_request(self, req_index: int) -> None:
+        if self.enable_adaptive_verification:
+            self.new_slots.append(req_index)
+
+    def reset_state(self) -> None:
+        """Forget everything learned so far (used after the warmup requests)."""
+        self.corpus.fill_(-1)
+        self.table.fill_(-1)
+        self.corpus_head.zero_()
+        self.doc_seq.zero_()
+        self.num_docs = 0
+        self.accept_stats.zero_()
+        self.last_bucket.fill_(-1)
+        self.last_valid.zero_()
+        self.num_steps = 0
+        self.new_slots.clear()
+
+    def init_cudagraph_manager(self, cudagraph_mode: CUDAGraphMode) -> None:
+        del cudagraph_mode
+
+    def capture(self) -> None:
+        return None
+
+    def on_requests_finished(self, finished_req_ids: Iterable[str]) -> None:
+        """Add finished responses to the corpus before their slots are freed."""
+        if not self.has_corpus:
+            return
+        req_states = self.req_states
+        # Sorted so every TP rank ingests documents in the same order. Starts
+        # come from the host copy of prompt_len: the device-visible copy is
+        # republished every step and may be reused for a new request before
+        # this kernel runs.
+        docs = []
+        for req_id in sorted(finished_req_ids):
+            slot = req_states.req_id_to_index.get(req_id)
+            if slot is None:
+                continue

+            # assistant header) so the first response tokens are indexed by
+            # the tokens that precede them.
+            start = max(int(req_states.prompt_len.np[slot]) - _PROMPT_CONTEXT, 0)
+            docs += [slot, start]
+        if not docs:
+            return
+        num_docs = len(docs) // 2
+        if self.num_docs + num_docs >= 1 << 31:
+            # Index entries pack doc_seq into 31 bits; start a new index (the
+            # corpus tokens stay, only their entries are dropped).
+            self.table.fill_(-1)
+            self.doc_seq.zero_()
+            self.num_docs = 0
+        self.num_docs += num_docs

+        token_ids = self.req_states.all_token_ids.gpu
+        _suffix_ingest_kernel[
+            (num_docs, triton.cdiv(self.max_model_len, _INGEST_BLOCK))
+        ](
+            token_ids,
+            token_ids.stride(0),
+            docs_gpu,
+            num_docs,
+            req_states.total_len.gpu,
+            self.corpus,
+            self.corpus_len,
+            self.corpus_head,
+            self.doc_seq,
+            self.ingest_out[0:1],
+            self.ingest_out[1:2],
+            self.table,
+            HASH_MUL=_HASH_MUL,
+            NUM_BUCKETS=self.num_buckets,
+            SLOTS=_BUCKET_SLOTS,
+            BLOCK=_INGEST_BLOCK,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+        self.corpus_head.copy_(self.ingest_out[0:1])
+        self.doc_seq.copy_(self.ingest_out[1:2])
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def propose(
+        self,
+        input_batch: InputBatch,
+        attn_metadata: Any,
+        slot_mappings: Any,
+        last_hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        aux_hidden_states: list[torch.Tensor] | None,

+        mm_inputs: tuple[list[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+        is_profile: bool = False,
+        num_speculative_tokens: int | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        num_reqs = input_batch.num_reqs
+        if dummy_run:
+            return self.drafts[:num_reqs]
+
+        token_ids = self.req_states.all_token_ids.gpu
+        total_len = self.req_states.total_len.gpu

+            if mask is not None:

+

+            self.num_steps += 1

+            token_ids,

+            self.num_valid,
+            self.accept_stats,
+            self.last_bucket,
+            self.last_valid,
+            self.draft_token_confidence_probs,
+            seeded,
+            HAS_CORPUS=self.has_corpus,
+            ADAPTIVE=self.enable_adaptive_verification,
+            HASH_MUL=_HASH_MUL,
+            NUM_BUCKETS=self.num_buckets,
+            SLOTS=_BUCKET_SLOTS,
+            MAX_DEPTH=self.max_depth,
+            DEPTH_PO2=triton.next_power_of_2(self.max_depth),
+            K=self.num_speculative_steps,
+            K_PO2=k_po2,
+            NB_PO2=max(1, triton.next_power_of_2(self.n_blocks)),
+            num_warps=4,

On my side, I'd like to join forces with you on integrating the SuffixGPU work into this PR's MRV2 implementation. The main piece I'd bring is the CUDA-graph'd draft path from #52097: bucketized draft graphs pre-captured at warmup, now wired onto the standard CUDAGraphWrapper/BatchDescriptor lifecycle (power-of-two buckets dispatched by batch size, graphs sharing the decoder graph pool, following the target model's graph mode, Triton JIT warmed at startup even with graphs off, dummy-run guard). The enabling trick is running the drafter kernels over the full slot space with a per-slot active mask instead of num_reqs-sized grids, so shapes stay step-invariant and each bucket is a single capture/replay — that per-step launch overhead is exactly what the low/mid-concurrency rows without adaptive verification bump into, so it should compose well with your trimming.
